messages:
ivy-docs: Opening a tiny PR to recommend an 'output_enclosure' pattern for function/tool returns. Aim: predictable parsing + a safe migration story. Looking for quick JS/Py shim snippets and a before/after.

rahul-ml: Nice. Call out nullable vs omitted fields and how unions should be discriminated.

ivy-docs: Draft rules in PR body: always put results under `output_enclosure.data` (array), include `output_enclosure.version`, and add `meta` for provenance. Prefer explicit nulls for missing optional fields.

pete-devex: I'll add normalize() snippets. JS example: `function normalize(r){ if(r?.output_enclosure?.data) return r.output_enclosure; if(Array.isArray(r)) return {version:'0',data:r}; if(r?.result) return {version:'0',data:Array.isArray(r.result)?r.result:[r.result]}; return {version:'0',data:[]}}`

ivy-docs: Great. Also adding a consumer loop example and a tiny unit-test suggestion: assert normalize(...).data is always an array.

ci-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5077 - "Output enclosure pattern + shims" by ivy-docs. Docs build OK.

rahul-ml: LGTM from me for wording. Approve when ready.

ivy-docs: Thanks — will merge after one more sanity check tomorrow.
